groups.why: Both say Dropbox is a poor general replacement for USB drives; s10 preserves the valid offline use case while warning against the broad claim.
Both identify ease of installation and setup as a barrier to using online storage.
The detailed latency and upload example explains why online drives can provide a poor user experience and lack practical offline access.
Together they make the case for launching with a focused product, then adding features after building a user base.
The second sentence states the benefit of the storytelling advice introduced in the first.
Both argue that user adoption is harder and more important than solving storage scale or cost.
The second sentence explains why many YC startups are less constrained by product costs.
Both identify the local folder and background sync as Dropbox's important distinction from typical online drives.
Both conclude that S3 costs and demand for free storage leave little room to charge profitably.
Both describe automatic saving and synchronization; s36 also preserves the added version-history detail.
